1.0.0.en: 1 The word of the LORD that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

1.1.0.en: Although Hosea is regarded chiefly as a prophet to Israel, that is, the northern kingdom, the Holy Bible dates his prophecy by the kings of Judah, mentioning only one of the kings of Israel. The man of God was called to serve the people of Israel and to warn them and forewarn them of captivity, yet his heart, enlarged with love for the salvation of all, rejoices in God's work with everyone, where God promises that "the children of Judah and the children of Israel [shall] be gathered together" [11]. He who serves God knows no limits to love, but desires to serve all and the salvation of everyone.

1.1.1.en: Some scholars see that Hosea mentioned only one king of Israel because the kings of Israel were wicked and unworthy of mention; he was content to mention this king who, though wicked, was honored with the title "saviour" (2 Kgs 14:27), and who was followed by a series of disturbances, assassinations and chaos that ended in captivity.

1.1.2.en: The prophet opens the book thus: "The word of the LORD that came unto Hosea the son of Beeri" [1], as though he wanted to affirm that what is in the book is not from himself but is "the word of the LORD," and he is only a bearer of the Lord's words and a true witness to them.

1.1.3.en: The prophet mentions his descent from his father "Beeri," which means "well." If Israel, as this book describes it, had become a ruined land, a barren wilderness, its fountain dried up and its spring withered (Hos 13:15), then it needs to sit with the Savior at the well, as happened with the Samaritan woman, to be refreshed from the spring of His water that never dries. What Hosea offers of words of salvation is from the divine well; whoever drinks of it shall never thirst (Jn 4:14).

1.2.0.en: 2 When the LORD first spoke to Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD." 3 So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived, and bare him a son, Some may wonder how God commands His prophet to be joined to an adulterous woman as his wife and to beget from her children of whoredom, for He says to him: "Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD" [2].

1.2.1.en: First: Some differ in interpreting the expression "a wife of whoredoms" (Hos 1:2); in English it is translated harlot and not adultress. Therefore some see that it does not mean merely an adulterous woman in the bodily way, according to the common understanding, but a woman who had consecrated her life to Baal, and so she is counted a harlot because of her attachment to Baal, especially since the worship of Baal was linked with the committing of adultery. There were women votaries who consecrated their lives to prostitution for the sake of Baal, and perhaps Gomer the daughter of Diblaim was of the class of these votaries.

1.2.2.en: In fact, the worship of idols was itself called adultery, harlotry, so that mere association with the worshippers of Baal was enough to give a person this title, even if he did not practice adultery. Perhaps this opinion is closer to the truth, for the majority of the Israelite women at that time, if not all of them, were attached to the worship of idols, so that it became difficult, perhaps impossible, for the prophet to find a wife except from among the worshippers of Baal, though not all of them practiced adultery bodily.

1.2.3.en: Second: A few scholars see that what is recorded in this chapter and the third chapter was only a vision or a symbolic story, presented to the people to reveal the ugliness of their fall and their turning away from the worship of the living God and their betrayal of Him instead of keeping the holy covenant with Him; and yet, with all this, God seeks them and wishes to bring them back to Himself, sanctifying them. But the majority of scholars see that what came here is a real event, and that God wanted the prophet to taste the great bitterness with Him because of Israel's deviation, and to declare to mankind the extent of God's care and love for man. As Abba Chaeremon says: [The divine Word described God's concern and care for us by the tongue of the prophet Hosea under the symbol of Jerusalem as a harlot, who turned aside in zeal full of ingratitude... He compares Jerusalem (the human soul) to an adulterous woman seeking another man, and compares His love for us to a man dying in love for his bride. For God's goodness and love are always declared to all men; they are overcome only by our ceasing to care for our salvation and by our fleeing from God's care for us, as though it were conquered by our evils. Therefore it is compared only to a man burning with the fire of love for his wife, who melts away in his love for her in proportion as he sees her treating him lightly and scornfully.]

1.2.4.en: Third: The majority of scholars see that the prophet married Gomer and loved her greatly, and then discovered what she was in the way of adultery (whether in the general bodily sense or merely association with the worship of Baal), and he kept her as his wife and did not divorce her; though some see that the prophet married her knowing her past, and that he consented to this because of the divine command, fulfilling in his life a symbolic picture of what was happening between God and His people.

1.2.5.en: Fourth: The word "Gomer" in Hebrew means the end of perfection, especially the perfection of failure, while "Diblaim" means a double cake of pressed figs or cakes of raisins. This kind of cake was used in the festivals of the worship of Baal, for it was said of the children of Israel that they "look to other gods, and love flagons of wine" (Hos 3:1), as though the eating of cakes stuffed with cakes of raisins or figs were closely linked with the worship of foreign gods. Thus the marriage of the prophet Hosea to Gomer the daughter of Diblaim points to his attachment to the people of Israel, who had reached the perfection of failure (Gomer), born of idolatrous worship and its abominations (Diblaim); or as though Israel, having become Gomer, is the daughter of Diblaim, that is, the daughter of the abominable festivals that spread throughout the land. She became like a cake offered to Baal, an abominable food and an unclean table for Satan and his followers!

1.2.6.en: Just as Gomer remained in her evil, bearing children of whoredom in spite of her marriage to a pure man and a blessed prophet, so Israel remained in its spiritual adultery in spite of God's declarations to it of His union with it. Hosea was not defiled because of Gomer; rather, Gomer came under a harsher judgment because of her marriage to the prophet unless she repented and returned in purity to her husband. So if Israel does not return to God in faith, its punishment will be more severe and more bitter!

1.2.7.en: St. Jerome sees in Gomer the harlot a symbolic picture of the Church, for he says: [What shall I say of the prophet's marriage to a harlot, who is a type of the Church gathered either from the Gentiles or from the Jews? She was first raised up by Abraham from among the worshippers of idols, and now she has denied the Savior and proved herself unfaithful to Him. Therefore she is deprived for a long time of her altar, her priests and her prophets, and remains many days until she returns to her first husband (Hos 2:7; 3:1), for when the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, Israel will be saved (Rom 11:25-26).]

1.2.8.en: And St. John Chrysostom says: [As in ancient times they took harlots as wives, so God received the nature that had played the harlot as His bride (without corruption), and the prophets declared from the beginning that this had happened with respect to the Jewish synagogue (Jer 3; Ezek 23:4-5, 11). But this bride was ungrateful toward her husband, whereas the Church, being saved from the evils she received from her fathers, continued to embrace her Bridegroom.]

1.2.9.en: The Lord says to Hosea: "for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD" [1], and the Greek translation reads: "for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD," as though whoredom were man's natural state when he leaves the Lord and is loosed from union with the eternal Bridegroom of his soul. It is remarkable that God does not say, "for Israel," but says, "for the land," and as we saw in the introduction, Israel, by bowing down toward earthly things, became an earth without heaven. I say that when we cleave to the dust we hear the divine voice: "for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return" (Gen 3:19), and we return to where the heart desired and turned. But if we put off the old earthy man whom we put on by our belonging to the earthy Adam, and put on the new man who is in the image of our heavenly Jesus, we hear the divine voice: "For you are heaven, and to heaven you shall return." I have borne the heavenly One in you, and your inner man has become heaven; therefore you return to where you desired and to what you have become, to heaven itself!

1.2.10.en: Since we have become earth by leaving the heavenly Bridegroom, what does this Bridegroom, who loves His bride, do with us? He took our earthy body, but without corruption, and came down to our earth to which our heart clung, without temporal things having any place in His heart, but to make of us "a new heaven and a new earth" (Rev 21:1), the earth of which it was said that righteousness itself dwells in it, that is, the heavenly Lord, the secret of our justification.

1.3.0.en: 4 And the LORD said unto him, "Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel. 5 And it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the bow of Israel, in the valley of Jezreel." 6 And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, "Call her name Lo-ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away. 7 But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen." 8 Now when she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son. 9 Then said God, "Call his name Lo-ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.

1.3.1.en: The Lord did not ask him only to marry an adulterous woman, but to beget from her children of whoredom, whose names God appoints: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi. This does not mean that they were the fruit of adultery; rather, merely because they were born of an adulterous mother who was attached to Baal or to idolatry, they were counted children of whoredom, although they were the prophet's children, until they accept their father's message and reject the old spirit of their mother.

1.3.2.en: First: "Jezreel" means "God sows," the first child of Hosea and Gomer, and it indicates that the chastisements He sows in us are the fruit of our own work. Jezreel reminds us of what Jehu did to Joram the son of Ahab and the wicked Jezebel, who killed and inherited the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, and the dogs licked her blood in the very field she had seized (1 Kgs 9-10). She demanded the field by seizure and shed innocent blood to obtain it, so she received the desire of her heart; she received destruction in the same place, as the natural fruit of her actions. The Lord says of the children of Israel: "they were abominable like their love" (Hos 9:10). What man loves, he receives as its natural fruit. He who loved the passing earth and the corrupt desires of the flesh received corruption and became earth, and he who loved the heavenly, eternal God enjoys immortal life.

1.3.3.en: Second: "Lo-ruhamah" means (not pitied). When man does not have mercy on himself and falls under attachment to the worship of Baal, he cannot expect mercy from God, for despising God's longsuffering and mercy treasures up wrath against the day of wrath (Rom 2:5).

1.4.0.en: The Lord says: "For I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away. But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen" [6-7].

1.4.1.en: Israel was plunged into evil and withdrew from God its Savior; neither bow nor sword nor horses nor horsemen can save it. But Judah, which points to the Church of the New Testament, which is the body of Christ that came out of the tribe of Judah, has its salvation by the LORD its God.

1.5.0.en: He says of the Savior: "the LORD their God." On the one hand He ascribes Himself to them as their God if they are sanctified, taking pride in them, as He calls Himself the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob; and He does not ascribe Himself to the wicked, for He says to them: "I will not be your God" [9], and the Greek translation: "I am not Yahweh to you."

1.5.1.en: The Lord says: "I will save them by the LORD their God." The Speaker is the Father, speaking of the Son the Savior. As Father Novatian says: [If God says that He will save by God, and since He saves only by Christ, why should any man hesitate to call Christ God, since the Father declares it in the Holy Bible? Yes, if God the Father saves only by God, no one can be saved by God the Father unless he confesses that Christ is God, in whom and by whom God promises to grant His salvation.]

1.5.2.en: Third: "Lo-ammi" means (not my kinsman) or (not my people), for the word "ammi" in Chaldean means (people) or (tribe). If sin begets "no mercy," the bitterness of no mercy is the deprivation of man from belonging to God or God's not belonging to him. How can one who belongs to Baal belong to God? The most we enjoy is the delight of the new Jerusalem coming down from heaven (Rev 21:2), which is "the tabernacle of God with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God" (Rev 21:3).

1.6.0.en: 10 Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. 11 Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

1.6.1.en: God mixes chastisement with hope, for He declares here that His chastisements are not absolute and that their rejection is not total but only for a time. He waits for them to return to Him so that He may restore them in more splendor and glory, restoring them as one strong and great kingdom, enjoying adoption to Him, rooted in Him, with Him as its head, for He says: "Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel" [10-11].

1.6.2.en: In the midst of the bitter chastisement He gives a new promise: He enters with them into a new covenant that was fulfilled not by their return from captivity but rather by their enjoyment of the Messianic age, and these are its features:

1.6.3.en: First: "The number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered," as though He is fulfilling the promise He had earlier declared to Abraham: "and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the sand which is upon the sea shore" (Gen 22:17), the promise to which Jacob held fast: "And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude" (Gen 32:12).

1.6.4.en: Truly, "though he cause grief (by chastisements), yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies" (Lam 3:32); for in Christ Jesus our Lord the fainting soul and the dry bones are turned into an exceedingly great army (Ezek 37:10). She becomes, not like Jerusalem, "terrible as an army with banners" (Song 6:4), which the enemy of good with all his army and deceptions cannot ensnare for himself, but like many strong horses that draw the divine chariot in the procession of victory. Therefore her Bridegroom addresses her, saying: "I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots" (Song 1:9).

1.6.5.en: The Apostle says: "one day is with the Lord as a thousand years" (2 Pet 3:8), and the believer also, who is like a passing day, becomes in Christ Jesus like a thousand years, bearing the heavenly mark (a thousand) with strong and mighty powers in the Spirit; so instead of a day he becomes countless years, and instead of human weakness he bears the possibilities of Christ: His mind, His will, His traits and His glory!

1.6.6.en: This is the mark of the Messianic age, which has turned our human life into "life in Christ Jesus"; instead of humiliation we have the inner heavenly glory, and instead of temporal thinking we live in the heavenly things.

1.6.7.en: Second: Mercy does not stop at abundance in number and strength in quality, but what rejoices our heart is our belonging to God as His sons: "in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God." Instead of rejection we are counted sons and heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ the only-begotten Son! We have become children of the living God, alive by our living Father. The Jews had called dead Baal their father and his wife Ashtaroth their mother, and so they bore the dead nature of their parents. This promise was not given to the Jews alone, whom He will receive after their rejection at the end of the ages when they accept the Messiah the Savior, but it touches our life, we who are of Gentile origin, for we were rejected because of our rejection of Him, and now the door of sonship to Him has been opened to us. As St. Augustine says: [Even the Apostle understood this saying as a prophetic testimony concerning the calling of the Gentiles, who before did not belong to God. And since this people from the Gentiles became children of Abraham spiritually, they were rightly called "Israel," and therefore he goes on to say: "Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head."]

1.6.8.en: Third: God's surpassing mercies in the Messianic age are declared through our unity together in Christ Jesus the one Head, "and appoint themselves one head." By accepting faith in Christ Jesus and enjoying adoption to God through Baptism, they appoint themselves one head.

1.6.9.en: He does not say, "They gather together under one king," but He highlights the perfection of unity by the Savior's being a Head from whom the body cannot be separated! It is a surpassing love, and a bond between the Creator and His beloved creation that cannot be expressed!

1.6.10.en: Fourth: We are joined together in the heavenly Head, so we bear His upper nature and ascend from our earthy, earthly nature, for He says: "and they shall come up out of the land." As the Apostle says: "If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth" (Col 3:1-2), since we are not of the world (Jn 15:19), but our conversation is in heaven (Phil 3:20).

1.6.11.en: In Christ Jesus we ascend from our old earthly nature, to enjoy the new heavenly nature that is in the image of our Creator, truly singing: "Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD." It is an exodus not from the land of Egypt toward the promised land, but a new ascent from the earth that enslaved the soul and in which it accepted Pharaoh (the devil) as a king who humbles the people. It is an ascent under the leadership of the Lord Christ Himself, not to take us to Mount Sinai, where there are lightnings and thunders and the smoking mountain, but for union with the Lord Christ, the holy mountain, that He may bring us by His Holy Spirit into the bosom of His Father.

1.6.12.en: Fifth: He concludes the promise by saying: "for great shall be the day of Jezreel." After "Jezreel" represented a threat and bitterness, where God gives us the fruit of our sins as chastisement for us, "Jezreel" becomes a promise, for the word means "God sows," so He sows us with His own hands as a new, holy planting (Isa 6:13); He sows us as members of the body of His only-begotten Son, we are watered with the waters of the Holy Spirit and bear the righteousness of Christ within us. He feeds us from the pierced side, so that we draw the very life instead of the death that was ours. This is what God assures us: "And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon Lo-ruhamah; and I will say to Lo-ammi, Thou art my people; and he shall say, Thou art my God" (Hos 2:23).
